c.tagline: Beethoven's birthplace and West Germany's genteel former capital.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; Free Now and Uber dispatch the same licensed taxis, so prices are broadly similar and there is little street-hailing outside ranks and stations.

emergency.note: 112 reaches ambulance and fire across the EU; 110 is the direct police line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The Hauptbahnhof forecourt attracts a small drug-and-drink scene at night, and pickpockets work the pedestrian shopping streets when crowded.

hood_desc: The compact historic center around Munsterplatz, the Beethoven monument, the Romanesque Munster, the old market and Beethoven's birthplace house; walkable and where most visitors base themselves.
One of Germany's largest intact Gruenderzeit quarters, a graceful grid of 19th-century townhouses, tree-lined streets, cafes and little shops just south of the center.
A relaxed university quarter around the yellow Poppelsdorf Palace, its botanical gardens and the cafe-lined Clemens-August-Strasse, popular with students.
A green former spa town in the south with diplomatic villas, the hilltop Godesburg castle ruin, the elegant Redoute hall and a Rhine promenade.
The right-bank district facing the old town across the Rhine, a residential and riverside area with the best views back to the Munster and the Kennedy Bridge.

water.note: Tap water is strictly regulated and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Stadtbahn and buses run roughly 4:30am-1am, with night buses and weekend late services filling the gaps.
transit.pay: No transit card needed: buy tickets in the SWB or VRS app or from station and on-board machines (bank cards accepted) and keep them for inspection. A single city ride is about 3.20 EUR (~US$3.50) and a day ticket around 8 EUR on the VRS tariff; Stadtbahn lines 16 and 18 also run north to Cologne. Staying weeks? The Deutschland-Ticket (58 EUR/month) covers local transit nationwide.

landmarks: Beethoven-Haus
The birthplace of Ludwig van Beethoven is now a treasured museum housing the world's largest collection of the composer's manuscripts and personal artifacts.
Bonn Minster (Bonner Münster)
This towering Romanesque cathedral with its distinctive octagonal crossing tower is Bonn's oldest and most recognizable church, dating back nearly a thousand years.
Beethoven Monument
A grand bronze statue of Beethoven standing at the heart of Münsterplatz has been the city's beloved tribute to its most famous son since 1845.
Altes Rathaus (Old Town Hall)
This gorgeous pink-and-white Rococo town hall on the market square is one of Germany's prettiest civic buildings and a favorite photo backdrop.
Poppelsdorf Palace
This elegant baroque palace, connected to the city center by a chestnut-tree-lined avenue, now houses university collections and a lovely botanical garden.
Kennedy Bridge (Kennedybrücke)
One of Bonn's iconic Rhine crossings, this bridge offers classic photogenic views of the river and the city skyline against the Siebengebirge hills.
Haus der Geschichte
Germany's popular House of History museum vividly chronicles postwar German history and is one of Bonn's most-visited cultural institutions.
Museum Koenig
This grand natural history museum, where the founding constitutional council of West Germany once convened, blends striking architecture with world-class zoological exhibits.
Godesburg Castle Ruins
The dramatic medieval ruins atop a volcanic hill in Bad Godesberg offer sweeping views over the Rhine valley and one of the region's most romantic vistas.
University of Bonn Main Building
Housed in a former electoral palace along the Rhine, this stately baroque building is the majestic centerpiece of one of Germany's oldest universities.

train.note: Bonn Hauptbahnhof sits on the left-Rhine main line; frequent regional trains, the S-Bahn and Stadtbahn reach Koln Hbf in about 20-30 minutes, where the full high-speed and international network connects. Some ICE and IC services also call directly at Bonn, and the OeBB Nightjet between Amsterdam and Switzerland passes through overnight. Bonn-Siegburg station on the high-speed line, 15 minutes away by Stadtbahn 66, is the stop for the fastest ICE runs to Frankfurt (around 40 minutes).

bus.note: Long-distance coaches stop at the ZOB beside Bonn Hauptbahnhof, so the interchange with trains and the Stadtbahn is a two-minute walk. FlixBus tickets are online only; there is no counter. Cologne is 30 minutes away by coach, Brussels around 4h and Amsterdam about 5h, and many more European services can be picked up in Cologne.

intl.to: Konigswinter, Linz & the Middle Rhine (Germany) - sails from the Rhine quay by the Alter Zoll

ferry.note: Bonn is 200 km from the sea, so there is no ferry in the maritime sense, but scheduled Rhine boats are a genuine way to travel south into the Siebengebirge. KD sails from the quay below the Alter Zoll upstream to Konigswinter for the Drachenfels and on towards Linz and the Middle Rhine gorge, mainly between April and October with reduced sailings at the shoulders. Small local car and passenger ferries also cross the Rhine to Beuel and between Bad Godesberg and Konigswinter all year, and take vehicles without booking.
